utterance: Hi Mark, I'm Dr Smith. I see you've come in with a cough and fever for the last few days. Can you tell me more about when it started and how it's been going?
reply: It started three days ago with a dry, hacking cough. I have been burning up on and off, and didn't have a thermometer, but I was roasting. Since yesterday I am bringing stuff up that is a rusty, brownish colour, though it was clear at first. Also since yesterday, there is a sharp pain low down on the right side, round towards my back, which catches me when I take a deep breath or cough.

utterance: Have you been feeling short of breath at rest or when walking around, or noticed any frank blood in what you're coughing up? Also, have you had any shaking chills, dizziness, or trouble keeping fluids down?
reply: I only get puffed going up the stairs and on the way in from the car park, but sitting here I am alright, and there is no actual blood, just that rusty colour. The first night I was shaking under the doona with my teeth chattering, even though I was boiling. My head is clear, though my wife reckons I am just grumpy, and I have had no vomiting.

As for allergies, I reacted to penicillin when I was a kid by coming up in hives and having my lips swell, which is probably not on my file since I haven't needed antibiotics in years.

utterance:
Here is our plan to get you feeling better, Mark:

1. **What's going on**: The examination and chest X-ray confirm you have community-acquired pneumonia in the lower part of your right lung. The good news is that your oxygen levels, blood pressure, and breathing rate are all in a safe range, so this is classified as mild pneumonia and can be safely treated at home with antibiotic tablets.

2. **Antibiotic treatment**: Because you had hives and lip swelling with penicillin as a child—which is a serious allergy that I will add to your medical file today—we will avoid penicillin antibiotics. Instead, I have prescribed **doxycycline 100 mg, one tablet twice a day for 5 days**. Make sure to swallow each tablet with a full glass of water and food, and stay sitting or standing upright for at least 30 minutes afterwards so it doesn't irritate your food pipe. It can also make your skin more sensitive to the sun, so wear sunscreen if you go outside.

3. **Symptom relief and rest**: 
   - Take paracetamol regularly as directed on the pack to help bring down your fever and ease that sharp chest pain so you can take deep breaths and clear your chest. Avoid cough-suppressant medicines, as coughing up that phlegm helps clear your lung.
   - Rest at home and drink plenty of fluids. I will print you a medical certificate for the rest of the week off school. Keep in mind that while the fever should settle within a few days, feeling tired and having a mild cough can take a few weeks to fully clear.

4. **Follow-up**: I would like to review you here in **48 hours (2 days)** to make sure the antibiotics are working and your breathing and temperature are improving. We will also check in again in about 6 weeks to ensure you've made a full recovery.

5. **When to seek urgent help**: Please have your wife take you straight to the hospital Emergency Department or call 000 if you notice any warning signs—such as becoming short of breath at rest, trouble speaking in full sentences, feeling dizzy, faint, or confused, coughing up bright red blood, severe worsening chest pain, inability to keep fluids down, or if you feel you are getting worse rather than better over the next 24 to 48 hours.

Does that all make sense, or do you have any questions for me?
reply: That all makes sense, and I will just make sure I get those tablets into me and follow the instructions. I had better get home to bed now so I can get rid of this before exams.
